summary.en: Why real people don't always decide 'rationally', and how businesses use that.
summary.bs: Zašto stvarni ljudi ne odlučuju uvijek 'racionalno' i kako firme to koriste.

en.one: Loss aversion means losing something hurts about twice as much as gaining the same thing feels good.
en.explain: People work harder to avoid a loss than to get an equal gain. That is why free trials work: once you have the product, cancelling feels like losing it.
en.example: 'Save €50' gets less response than 'Don't lose €50' for the same energy-saving offer.
en.why: It helps you frame offers, guarantees and trials, and spot when fear of a loss is driving your own decisions.
en.mixup: Loss aversion is not just being careful. It makes people hold on to bad investments too long to avoid admitting a loss.

bs.one: Loss aversion (averzija prema gubitku) znači da gubitak boli otprilike duplo više nego što isti dobitak raduje.
bs.explain: Ljudi se više trude izbjeći gubitak nego dobiti jednak dobitak. Zato besplatne probe rade: kad jednom imaš proizvod, otkazivanje se čini kao gubitak.
bs.example: 'Uštedi 50 €' dobije manje odziva nego 'Nemoj izgubiti 50 €' za istu ponudu uštede energije.
bs.why: Pomaže ti oblikovati ponude, garancije i probe, i primijetiti kad strah od gubitka vodi tvoje odluke.
bs.mixup: Averzija prema gubitku nije samo opreznost. Tjera ljude da predugo drže loše investicije da ne priznaju gubitak.

en.one: Anchoring is when the first number people see shapes how they judge everything after.
en.explain: A high first price makes later prices seem cheap. Even random numbers can act as anchors. Sellers use it with 'was €200, now €120', and negotiators open with an ambitious first offer.
en.example: A menu lists a €60 steak at the top. The €28 pasta now looks reasonable, so more people order it.
en.why: Anchors shape what customers think is a fair price, and the first offer in a negotiation often sets the range.
en.mixup: An anchor does not have to be believable to work. Even an obviously high number pulls guesses toward it.

bs.one: Anchoring (efekat sidra) je kad prvi broj koji ljudi vide oblikuje kako procjenjuju sve poslije.
bs.explain: Visoka prva cijena čini kasnije cijene jeftinijim. Čak i nasumični brojevi mogu biti sidro. Prodavci to koriste s 'bilo 200 €, sada 120 €', a pregovarači otvaraju ambicioznom prvom ponudom.
bs.example: Na vrhu menija je biftek za 60 €. Pasta za 28 € sada izgleda razumno, pa je više ljudi naruči.
bs.why: Sidra oblikuju šta kupci smatraju fer cijenom, a prva ponuda u pregovorima često postavi okvir.
bs.mixup: Sidro ne mora biti uvjerljivo da bi radilo. Čak i očito previsok broj vuče procjene prema sebi.

en.one: A sunk cost is money or time already spent that you cannot get back. The fallacy is letting it push you to keep going with a bad plan.
en.explain: Good decisions look only at future costs and benefits. What is spent is spent either way. Yet people keep pouring money into failing projects 'because we've already invested so much'.
en.example: You spent €20,000 on an app that customers don't use. Spending another €10,000 'so the first €20,000 isn't wasted' is the sunk cost fallacy.
en.why: Recognising it saves you from throwing good money after bad.
en.mixup: Ignoring sunk costs does not mean ignoring lessons. Learn from what you spent, but don't let it decide what you do next.

bs.one: Sunk cost (nepovratni trošak) je novac ili vrijeme već potrošeno koje ne možeš vratiti. Zamka je kad te to tjera da nastaviš s lošim planom.
bs.explain: Dobre odluke gledaju samo buduće troškove i koristi. Potrošeno je potrošeno u svakom slučaju. Ipak, ljudi nastave ulijevati novac u projekte koji propadaju 'jer smo već toliko uložili'.
bs.example: Potrošio si 20.000 € na aplikaciju koju kupci ne koriste. Potrošiti još 10.000 € 'da prvih 20.000 € ne propadne' je zamka nepovratnog troška.
bs.why: Kad je prepoznaš, ne bacaš dobar novac za lošim.
bs.mixup: Ignorisati nepovratni trošak ne znači ignorisati lekcije. Uči iz onoga što si potrošio, ali ne daj da to odluči šta radiš dalje.

en.one: A nudge is a small change in how a choice is shown that steers people without forbidding anything.
en.explain: Defaults are the strongest nudge: most people stay with what is pre-selected. Others are reminders, putting healthy food at eye level, or showing what neighbours do. People are still free to choose otherwise.
en.example: When a company makes pension saving the default and staff must opt out, many more people save.
en.why: Small design choices on your website, forms or shop shelves can change what customers do far more than price cuts.
en.mixup: A nudge is not a hidden trick. Tricks that hide costs or make cancelling hard are 'dark patterns' and can be illegal.

bs.one: Nudge (blagi podsticaj) je mala promjena u načinu prikaza izbora koja usmjerava ljude, a ništa ne zabranjuje.
bs.explain: Zadane opcije su najjači nudge: većina ljudi ostane na onome što je unaprijed označeno. Drugi su podsjetnici, zdrava hrana u visini očiju ili prikaz šta rade komšije. Ljudi i dalje slobodno biraju drugačije.
bs.example: Kad firma postavi penzionu štednju kao zadanu, a radnici se moraju sami odjaviti, mnogo više ljudi štedi.
bs.why: Mali dizajnerski izbori na tvom sajtu, formularima ili policama mogu promijeniti ponašanje kupaca više od sniženja.
bs.mixup: Nudge nije skriveni trik. Trikovi koji skrivaju troškove ili otežavaju otkazivanje su 'dark patterns' i mogu biti nezakoniti.

concepts.youtubeQuery: social proof and herd behavior explained

en.one: Herd behaviour is when people copy what others do instead of deciding on their own. Social proof is using that: 'others chose this, so it must be good'.
en.explain: When we are unsure, the crowd feels like a safe guide. This drives reviews, 'bestseller' labels and queues outside restaurants. In markets, it can create bubbles when everyone buys because everyone else is buying.
en.example: Two restaurants side by side: the one with a queue gets even more guests, even if the food is the same.
en.why: Reviews, testimonials and customer counts are some of the strongest sales tools you have.
en.mixup: Popular is not the same as good. A crowd can be wrong, as crashes after price bubbles show.

bs.one: Herd behaviour (ponašanje krda) je kad ljudi kopiraju druge umjesto da sami odluče. Social proof (društveni dokaz) je korištenje toga: 'drugi su ovo izabrali, mora biti dobro'.
bs.explain: Kad nismo sigurni, gomila se čini kao siguran vodič. To pokreće recenzije, oznake 'najprodavanije' i redove ispred restorana. Na tržištima može stvoriti balone kad svi kupuju jer svi drugi kupuju.
bs.example: Dva restorana jedan do drugog: onaj s redom dobije još više gostiju, iako je hrana ista.
bs.why: Recenzije, preporuke i broj kupaca su neki od najjačih alata prodaje koje imaš.
bs.mixup: Popularno nije isto što i dobro. Gomila može griješiti, kao što pokazuju padovi nakon cjenovnih balona.

en.one: The scarcity effect is when people want something more because it seems rare or about to run out.
en.explain: 'Only 2 left', 'offer ends tonight' and limited editions all use it. Scarcity makes us fear missing out and decide faster, often with less thinking.
en.example: A hotel site shows 'Only 1 room left at this price!' and you book within minutes.
en.why: Honest scarcity, like real limited stock, can boost sales, and knowing the trick helps you resist it as a buyer.
en.mixup: Do not confuse this with scarcity in economics, which simply means resources are limited. This is a feeling that makes things seem more valuable.

bs.one: Scarcity effect (efekat oskudice) je kad ljudi nešto više žele jer izgleda rijetko ili pred nestankom.
bs.explain: 'Još samo 2', 'ponuda ističe večeras' i ograničena izdanja to koriste. Oskudica izaziva strah da ćemo propustiti i tjera nas da brže odlučimo, često uz manje razmišljanja.
bs.example: Sajt hotela pokaže 'Još samo 1 soba po ovoj cijeni!' i ti rezervišeš za par minuta.
bs.why: Iskrena oskudica, kao stvarno ograničene zalihe, može povećati prodaju, a kad znaš trik, lakše mu odoliš kao kupac.
bs.mixup: Ne miješaj ovo s oskudicom u ekonomiji, koja samo znači da su resursi ograničeni. Ovo je osjećaj zbog kojeg stvari izgledaju vrijednije.

q.en: You've spent €20,000 on a failing project. What should decide whether you spend €10,000 more?
q.bs: Potrošio si 20.000 € na projekat koji propada. Šta treba odlučiti da li ćeš potrošiti još 10.000 €?

options.en: How embarrassing it is to stop

explain.en: The €20,000 is a sunk cost. It is gone either way, so only the future counts.
explain.bs: 20.000 € je nepovratni trošak. Nema ga u svakom slučaju, pa se računa samo budućnost.

q.en: A shop shows 'was €200, now €120'. Which effect does the €200 use?
q.bs: Radnja pokaže 'bilo 200 €, sada 120 €'. Koji efekat koristi tih 200 €?

explain.en: The first number (€200) becomes an anchor that makes €120 feel cheap.
explain.bs: Prvi broj (200 €) postaje sidro zbog kojeg 120 € izgleda jeftino.

q.en: Pension saving is set as the default and staff must opt out. Many more people save. This is…
q.bs: Penziona štednja je postavljena kao zadana, a radnici se moraju odjaviti. Mnogo više ljudi štedi. To je…

explain.en: Changing the default steers behaviour without removing choice: a nudge.
explain.bs: Promjena zadane opcije usmjerava ponašanje bez oduzimanja izbora: to je nudge.

q.en: Why do free trials convert so well?
q.bs: Zašto besplatne probe tako dobro pretvaraju korisnike u kupce?

options.en: Cancelling feels like losing something you have
options.bs: Otkazivanje se čini kao gubitak nečega što imaš

explain.en: Loss aversion: once you have it, giving it up hurts more than not having had it.
explain.bs: Averzija prema gubitku: kad nešto imaš, odricanje boli više nego da ga nikad nisi imao.
